text:
maria: Heads-up — private deploy in customer-vpc-33 is showing intermittent p99 spikes (generator routes) around 06:10–06:20 UTC. Not steady CPU, but requests queueing at the egress path.

devon: any recent kernel/patch changes on those nodes? Could be a fallback kernel path kicking in under certain seq len.

maria: No kernel upgrade last night. But we rolled out a runtime tweak for kernel-selection heuristics yesterday (canary) that changes which GEMM/kernels we pick for int8 quant routes.

jonathan: I pulled a flamegraph from the offending pod at 06:14 — the runtime spent ~35% more time in "fallback_attention" kernel compared to baseline, and batching spikes correlate with the tail. Uploaded profile snippet to the perf bucket.

liam: FYI I also see a large burst of retransmits on the NAT gateway at the same time. bytes_out spiked and MSS drop counters on the firewall increased. Could be fragmentation/MTU related when we send larger batched payloads.

anya: That matches a theory: if KV cache misses force full-context resends the request size jumps (we saw a KVcache regen storm in logs). Large POST payloads + SNAT hairpin + firewall MTU clamp = blackhole/rto.

maria: Reproduced locally by forcing a KV miss + batching size 64 on a private node: traceroute to metrics endpoint shows first hop MSS clamped by 1400, then retransmits.

devon: Can you paste the tcpdump/cmd you used?

maria: Ran: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.5.2.1 and tcp and port 443 -w /tmp/egress.pcap
sudo iptables -t mangle -L -v
```
Seen PSH flags, then dup ACKs, then RTO.

jonathan: On the runtime side, when fallback_attention triggers it increases sequence memory and we do a synchronous KV prefetch which serializes and coalesces many small calls into a single big outgoing packet (payload ~18KB). That easily exceeds common MTU 1500 after TLS overhead if MSS is clamped by firewall.

liam: Customer firewall has an explicit MSS clamp for VPN users, and their SNAT is hairpinning internal requests through perimeter NAT for certain subnets — classic path MTU+hairpin recipe for trouble.

anya: What about conntrack? Are we seeing table churn? ops-bot: conntrack_count=78k -> 95k at spike; eviction events logged.

sre-oncall: Running temporary mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch to 24 on private nodes 2) disable the kernel-selection canary that forces fallback_attention on quantized models 3) add egress pacing to avoid giant single POSTs. Rolling now to the canary set.

maria: Thanks. After throttling batch_size and disabling the canary the p99 returned to baseline within ~4 minutes. But we should fix root cause not just mitigate.

devon: Action items: (a) runtime — add bounded chunking for outgoing requests when KV regen creates large payloads (b) kernel-selection — add metric + circuit to avoid choosing fallback kernel if it will blow up memory/batching behavior (c) infra — work with customer to remove hairpin SNAT for internal metrics path or ensure MSS passthrough.

jonathan: I'll attach the profiling diff showing which instruction paths trigger fallback_attention; we might be able to tune thresholds so kernel-selection stays on optimized path for common sequence lengths.

liam: I'll open a ticket with the firewall vendor about the MSS clamp behavior and propose a pinhole for internal VPC egress to skip MSS rewriting.

anya: Also add a regression test in the private-deployment suite to simulate KV cache storm + large batch and assert no p99 > 2x baseline.

maria: +1. Will follow up with a short postmortem once all actions are done. Thank you everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident annotated: severity=medium, ticket=INFRA-4721, runbook=egress-mtu-hairpin.
